result.summary: Refactors peer send pause tracking in CNode by removing the separate boolean flag and encoding the paused state directly into a single atomic timestamp. Transitions are consolidated into CNode accessors, allowing inactivity checks to read pause status and duration in a single snapshot. Associated test harness resets are centralized into ProcessMessagesOnce.
result.problem: Peer send pause status was tracked across two separate variables: a boolean flag and a start timestamp. Logic to synchronize these variables was duplicated across message queueing and socket send paths, and inactivity checks read them non-atomically.
evidence: Author description: 'Message queueing and socket sends each duplicate the transition logic that keeps the two in sync, and the inactivity check (which needs both), reads them separately.'
result.scope_notes: Follow-up refactor to recently merged PR #36667; the diff was omitted from the prompt.
result.card: Unifies peer send pause tracking by replacing a separate boolean flag and start timestamp with a single atomic timestamp where an epoch value represents unpaused state. This removes duplicate state transition logic between message queueing and socket sends and enables atomic reads by the inactivity check. It is an internal refactor following up on PR #36667.

risk.why: Bugs in send-pause state transitions could cause peers to improperly timeout or stall socket sends, degrading P2P network connectivity.
